$comment: Wikidata Q-ids referenced by hand-written SPARQL. NONE of these could be confirmed from this build environment, so every one carries expectedLabel and verified:false. This file exists so that verification at egress is a single pass over one file rather than a hunt through query strings. Queries that depend on an entity are written to degrade to an empty result rather than a wrong result when the id is wrong — an empty cabinet renders as 'not recorded', which is honest, where a wrong id could silently attach another country's ministries.

minister.usedBy: cabinet query, as the superclass reached by P279* when finding ministerial positions
minister.fallback: The cabinet query UNIONs this path with P208 (executive body) + P361 (part of), so a wrong id here degrades coverage rather than producing wrong rows.
minister.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 by the check that was already implied by expectedLabel: Q83307 resolves to "minister" with 178 instances, which matches. The doubt recorded here was unfounded — but nobody knew that, because the doubt had been written down and never measured. The court entry beside it was wrong in exactly the same posture and stayed wrong for as long.

courtOfLastResort.usedBy: judiciary query, as a fallback class when P209 is absent
courtOfLastResort.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-15. Was Q1513611, which is "Supreme Court of Ghana" — a specific court, not a class, with ZERO instances anywhere in Wikidata, so the fallback branch could never match for any country. Q190752 is "supreme court" (highest court in a jurisdiction), with 272 instances and used by 99 countries' P209 courts. The expectedLabel recorded here was always right; only the qid was wrong, and comparing the two would have caught it.

properties.$comment: Properties are far more stable than items and are used directly in the queries. Listed for review, not for lookup.
properties.P1313: office held by head of government
properties.P1410: number of representatives in an organization/legislature
properties.P1906: office held by head of state
